OpenECS 0.2.0 adds standard plugins that your plugins can build on: drawing, user interfaces, character grids, images, sound, networking, 3D models and files. It also adds a settings window, a launcher, pop-out windows and popups, and simpler settings and keys.

It comes out with the first releases of two repositories that OpenECS ships, each described in its own release:

- [OpenECS-std 0.2.0](https://github.com/omerfuyar/OpenECS-std/releases/tag/v0.2.0): the standard plugins, the settings window and the launcher.
- [OpenECS-examples 0.2.0](https://github.com/omerfuyar/OpenECS-examples/releases/tag/v0.2.0): seventeen examples, from a first Lua plugin to a drawing tool, and one for each standard plugin.

This is still an early release. Plugins made for 0.1.0 need the changes under "What will break".

## What you can do

**Start from the launcher.**

- Run `OpenECS` with no preset, and the launcher lists your presets and saved sessions. Click one, or choose it with the arrows and Return.
- Run `OpenECS --help` to see the options. Each has a short form: `-p` for `--preset`, `-s` for `--session`, `-f` for `--fresh`, and so on.

**Change settings in a window.**

- Press Alt+W, then `,` to open the settings window. It lists every setting of the core and the plugins, with a control for each type.
- A value that does not fit its setting's type shows as wrong, and is not saved.
- The window writes your settings file, `~/.config/openecs/settings.lua`.

**Arrange panels across windows.**

- Press Alt+W, then P to move a panel into a window of its own. Sessions keep these windows.
- Press Alt+W, then W to choose a workspace from a menu.

**Keep your work, when you want to.**

- A tool now starts from its preset each time. To get your last session back at the next start, set `["ecs.keepSession"] = true` in your settings file.
- Alt+W, then S saves the session to a file whenever you want.

**Build plugins on the standard plugins.** They ship in the archive's `plugins/` folder: draw, ui, tty, image, audio, net, gltf and fs. [OpenECS-std 0.2.0](https://github.com/omerfuyar/OpenECS-std/releases/tag/v0.2.0) says what each does. A standard plugin needs nothing but OpenECS, so copying its folder installs it.

**Use other plugins' functions easily.**

- In Lua, `local draw = require("draw")` gives the functions of the plugin `draw`, when your manifest depends on it.
- `OpenECS --definitions FOLDER` writes a file for each loaded plugin: `NAME.lua` for your editor's completion and checks, and `NAME.h` for C plugins, with typed functions.
- Function signatures can name their parameters, such as `void(string path, float volume)`, and those names show in your editor.

**Write richer panels.**

- Panels can take typed text, with the input method's help, such as for accented letters.
- Panels can open popups: menus and tooltips next to a part of the panel.
- `surface:fill(x, y, width, height, color)` in Lua, and `ECSSurface_Fill` in C, fill a rectangle in one call.
- `ecs.plugin.folder` gives the folder a plugin was loaded from, so it can read its own files.
- Lua plugins have all of Lua's standard libraries: `io` reads and writes files, and `os` renames and removes them. The fs plugin lists and makes folders.
- Add `---@type ecs.Preset` or `---@type ecs.Manifest` above the `return` of a preset or a manifest, and your editor completes and checks it.

**Learn from the examples.** The archive's `examples/` folder holds them, each a preset with its plugins and a test; [OpenECS-examples 0.2.0](https://github.com/omerfuyar/OpenECS-examples/releases/tag/v0.2.0) lists them. Run one with `OpenECS --fresh --preset examples/1_hello/preset.lua`; `--fresh` starts it from its preset, even when `ecs.keepSession` is on.

## Small fixes

- A failed start shows the step that failed, the file, the error, and where the log file is.
- A missing plugin, or one that fails to load, is logged as an error, and the program goes on.
- While you type in a panel, letter keys never run key bindings.
- The session's save dialog suggests a file named after the preset.
- Closing a pop-out window frees the textures of its panels first, so a panel that moved out of it never draws with a freed texture.

## What will break

**Keys.** Every keys table has one shape now. A field is a key combination, and its value is the name of a function to run, or `false` to remove the key. The field `prefix` holds the keys after Alt+W, and a field named after a panel type holds that panel type's keys:

```lua
keys = {
  ["Ctrl+N"] = "notes.new",
  prefix = { ["N"] = "notes.new" },
  ["notes.editor"] = { ["Ctrl+B"] = "notes.bold" },
}
```

- In settings files and presets, move the keys of `ecs.prefixKeys` into `keys.prefix`.
- `ECSKey_Bind(plugin, panelType, key, function)` and `ecs.input.bind(panelType, key, function)` now take a key combination, such as `"Ctrl+N"`, instead of the name of a key setting.

**Settings.**

- There are three settings layers: the defaults, the preset, and your settings file.
- A `key` or `color` value that cannot be read is reported, and the default is used. Colours are written `"#RRGGBB"` or `"#RRGGBBAA"`.

**Sessions.** A tool no longer restores its last session unless `ecs.keepSession` is on.

**Command line.** An unknown option, or an option without its value, is an error, and OpenECS exits with status 2.

**Plugins and presets moved.**

- The sketch plugins and their preset are now the example `examples/12_sketch/`.
- The standard plugins, the settings window and the launcher are in [OpenECS-std](https://github.com/omerfuyar/OpenECS-std), and the examples are in [OpenECS-examples](https://github.com/omerfuyar/OpenECS-examples). Both are submodules of OpenECS, in `std/` and `examples/`. Clone OpenECS with `--recursive`.

**Building from source.**

- `shuild -b TYPE` chooses the build type: `debug`, `release`, `relwithdebinfo` or `minsizerel`. The `--static` and `--dynamic` options are gone.
- The build goes to `build/TYPE/`, such as `build/Release/`.
- The build builds the standard plugins of `std/` too, with their own `shuild.c`; `-n` leaves them out. `-e` builds the examples of `examples/` the same way.
- A test loads only the plugins its preset names, and each repository runs its own tests: `test.sh` with `std` or `examples` runs theirs.

## Downloads

- `openecs-0.2.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`: the program with SDL's libraries, its plugins, presets and examples, the plugin interface, and the licenses. Unpack it and run `OpenECS`.
- `openecs-0.2.0-source.tar.gz`: the source with every library it uses. GitHub's own "Source code" archives leave the libraries out, so use this one to build.
- `SHA256SUMS`: checksums of the archives.

Only Linux on x86_64 has a build. It needs glibc 2.38 or later, such as Ubuntu 24.04 or Fedora 39.

OpenECS is under the zlib license.
